court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Integrated Finance Company vs M/S. Ravishankar Industries

parties.respondent_defendant: M/s. Ravishankar Industries Private Ltd., Respondent(s)

facts_of_case: Criminal Appeal filed against the judgment passed in CCNo.6199 of 1998, dated 20.07.2005 by the learned XVII Metropolitan Magistrate, Saidapet, Chennai.

legal_principles.principle: When a subsequent agreement has been entered into, the majority of the cheques which are supposed to be issued in respect of the original agreements cannot still be filled up and presented by the complainant organization.
legal_principles.held: The trial court held that when a subsequent agreement has been entered into, the majority of the cheques which are supposed to be issued in respect of the original agreements cannot still be filled up and presented by the complainant organization.

legal_principles.principle: The complainant has failed to prove that there existed a legally enforceable liability.
legal_principles.held: The trial court held that the complainant, having entered into the lease cum hire purchase agreement, had also failed to prove the delivery of machinery to the accused company.

legal_principles.principle: When the entire case is in doubt, it is unsafe for the court to convict the accused and give the benefit of the doubt.
legal_principles.held: The trial Court found that when the entire case is in doubt as to for which agreement the cheque has been issued and whether there exists a liability, etc., it was unsafe for the court to convict the accused and gave the benefit of the doubt.

keywords: High Court of Judicature at Madras
use_for_drafting: drafting a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
defending against a cheque bounce case
advising on criminal proceedings for cheque dishonour
